$comment: Corpus for the tier-1 `default_system_prompt_equivalence` family (v4 `baa85e19b`, bug 154 — `lib/characters/default-system-prompt.ts`). Rows 1-7 are v4's own five test vectors from `__tests__/unit/lib/characters/default-system-prompt.test.ts`, verbatim (the fifth asks three shapes, carried as three rows). The rest ask the shapes that suite does not: JS truthiness on both the column and the flag, the strict-equality column match against a non-string column, duplicate flags, and the content form's empty-string arm. Each row is a whole `character` object passed to the resolver; the oracle emits the resolved prompt OBJECT, its id, and the CONTENT form (v4 `lib/chat/initialize.ts:146` transcribed — `getDefaultSystemPrompt` is not exported, so its driving proof is `chat_context_init_equivalence`'s `empty_content_default` case).

cases.note: v4 test 1 — prefers the column when it names a prompt the character has.
v4 test 2 — falls through to the isDefault flag when the column is null.
v4 test 3 — THE FIX: a column naming a prompt that is gone falls through to the flag.
v4 test 4 — falls through to the first prompt when nothing is marked default.
v4 test 5 — a character with no prompts at all.
v4 test 5 — the bare `{}`: no systemPrompts key at all.
v4 test 5 — `systemPrompts: null` with a column: the `?? []` wins and the column is never consulted.
§S.2 extra — `''` is JS-falsy, so the column is not consulted at all.
§S.2 extra — `find` stops at the FIRST truthy flag.
§S.2 extra — no `isDefault` key anywhere plus a stale column: `prompts[0]`.
The column key omitted entirely (not null) — `undefined` is falsy.
JS truthiness on the column: `false` never reaches the find.
A truthy NON-STRING column: the `===` match cannot succeed against a string id, so it falls through exactly as a falsy column would.
JS truthiness on the column: `0` is falsy.
JS truthiness on the FLAG: `find(p => p.isDefault)` takes a non-empty string.
JS truthiness on the FLAG: `0` does not count, so this falls to `prompts[0]`.
JS truthiness on the FLAG: an explicit `null` does not count.
The column outranks the flag when it names an existing prompt — the whole point of recording it.

The CONTENT form's `??`: a resolved prompt whose content is `''` answers `''` and does NOT fall through to the first prompt's content. This is the arm the pre-fix `||` chain got wrong; its DRIVING proof is `chat_context_init_equivalence`'s `empty_content_default` case.
The CONTENT form's `?.content ?? ''` when the key is absent entirely.
The commonest real shape after a delete-the-last-default: one prompt, no flag, no column.
The prompt resolves (the object comes back) but has no `id`: the Id form's `?.id ?? null` answers null while the prompt itself is non-null — the two forms disagree by design.
